# Remaining TODOs for the GEOS-agent paper

*Generated by research-copilot. Captures the open items so progress
isn't lost across conversations.*

## High priority — recommended for camera-ready

### 1. Clean DSv4 re-run with native-plugin-prefix bug fixed

**What**: Re-run F0, F4, F6, SE on `deepseek-v4-flash` × test-17 × 3 seeds with the fixed orchestrator gate (commit `000b4ba`). Default-off harness env (`GEOS_HOOK_POSTTOOLUSE` unset).

**Why**: The autocamp $R = -0.033$ main effect was contaminated by the buggy prefix on $R^{-}$ cells (F2, F4, F6, F8, F11). A clean re-run replaces these contaminated headline numbers with bug-fixed equivalents.

**How large is the contamination?** The team's own `abl_c9_no_prefix` cell measured it directly over **3 seeds $\times$ 17 tasks** (`docs/ablation_C2_vs_C9.md`): C2 (prefix) $0.9134$ vs C9 (no prefix) $0.9170$, $\Delta = +0.0036$, zero big-swing tasks ($|\Delta| \geq 0.10$). So on DSv4 the prefix effect is $\approx +0.004$ — null. It is **not** $+0.24$ and it was **not** a single seed. The $+0.24$ figure that appeared in earlier notes is the C1$\to$C2 build-up lift that C9 was created to *explain* ($0.6713 \to 0.8649 \to 0.9134$); the "prefix drives it" hypothesis was refuted. Do not cite $+0.24$ as the prefix effect anywhere, least of all in a rebuttal.

**Cost**: ~1.5h wall-clock at workers=4, ~$0.50 in DSv4 API spend.

**Expected impact**: Vanilla and SE should be unchanged (their factor settings make them prefix-irrelevant); F4 (X+M) may shift up by 1–3pp; F6 (S+X without memory) similarly. The X+M-vs-Vanilla relative ranking stays intact (both are $R^-$ and the bug applies asymmetrically — Vanilla has plugin disabled and so never sees the prefix).

**Launcher**: extend `scripts/launch_autocamp_phase2.sh` or write `scripts/launch_postfix_dsv4.sh` patterned on it.

### 2. Multi-seed cross-model on minimax and gemini

**What**: Repeat the cross-model panel (Vanilla / X+M / SE on `minimax-m2.7` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`) at $n=3$ seeds.

**Why**: Tightens single-seed effect-size estimates. The $+0.046$ minimax X+M lift and $+0.029$ gemini X+M lift are point estimates without σ; multi-seed lets us claim significance.

**Cost**: gemini is the bottleneck. Single-seed gemini × 3 cells × 17 tasks cost ~$14; tripling = ~$42. Single-seed minimax × 3 cells × 17 tasks cost ~$8.62; tripling = ~$26. Total ~$68.

**Decision rule**: include in camera-ready if budget allows; v1 can ship with single-seed.

## Medium priority

### 4. Investigate gemini × SE regression below Vanilla

**What**: Why does SE on gemini score $0.757$ (below gemini Vanilla's $0.768$)? This is the only backbone where SE is anti-correlated with Vanilla.

**How**: Inspect a few gemini × SE failure trajectories. Check if the SE plugin's RAG MCP calls are timing out, if cheatsheet text is steering gemini wrong, or if it's a noise-at-$n=1$ artefact.

**Quick fix**: re-run gemini × SE at $n=3$ seeds; if the regression persists, dig deeper.

### 5. OpenCode harness integration

**What**: Build a thin wrapper for OpenCode (currently no integration). Run Vanilla + X+M-equivalent × DSv4-flash × test-17 × 3 seeds.

**Why**: The cross-harness panel currently has only one alternative harness (OpenHands). A second alternative would strengthen the "X+M generalises across harnesses" claim.

**Cost**: 4–8 hours of integration build (most of it in mapping our MCP tool registration to OpenCode's tool model and porting the parse-check + xmllint validation hook to OpenCode's analogue). Then ~2h experiment time, ~$1 in API.

**Decision**: Drop for v1 if integration cost is high; flag as v2 follow-up.

### 6. GEOS execution-correctness ladder

**What**: Run a sample of agent-produced decks through actual GEOS execution. Even a tiny panel (5 tasks × 2 cells × 1 seed) converts TreeSim from a structural-similarity proxy into a runnability ladder.

**Why**: A reviewer asking "can the agent's deck actually run?" lands a fair hit on TreeSim alone. A small "X% of decks pass GEOS's parser; Y% complete a single timestep" panel would close this.

**Cost**: Wall depends on GEOS build availability. Probably 1–2 days of integration setup if no GEOS build is currently usable in our infra.

### 7. Cross-section consistency hook (new adapter from bottleneck analysis)

**What**: Implement an adapter that validates `<ElementRegion materialList="X,Y,Z">` entries against `<Constitutive>` block names. Run as a new cell.

**Why**: The bottleneck analysis surfaced this as the main category surviving X+M (`bad_attribute_value`-class failures from cross-section mismatches). Building an adapter that fixes it converts bottleneck-analysis-as-observation into bottleneck-analysis-as-design-output.

**Cost**: ~1 day of implementation + 3 seeds of running. Increases method novelty for main-track submission.

## Low priority / nice-to-have

### 8. Held-out-10 cross-model

Currently cross-model is on test-17 only. Held-out-10 is the harder set; running cross-model there would show whether the X+M ranking holds on hard tasks across backbones. Skip if the v1 page budget is tight.
